exception.reason: UCR offers genuine biochemistry, molecular-cell biology, life-science laboratory work, environmental geochemistry, resource recovery and quantitative methods. These do not form the sustained synthetic, analytical, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry, thermodynamics, quantum/structural study, synthesis laboratories and chemistry research that define this degree. The biomedical candidate is mainly biology, disease and cognition; the environmental candidate studies existing biological and Earth systems and assesses resource use rather than designing and synthesising chemical molecules or materials. General data, life-cycle analysis, renewable-energy design and adjacent laboratories cannot supply the missing defining chemistry. No sufficiently close complete UCR programme is retained.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud Chemistry studies how molecular structure determines properties and reactions. Its programme combines synthetic, analytical, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry with mathematics, physics, extensive laboratory training and an individual research internship.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers genuine biochemistry, molecular biology, laboratory work, environmental geochemistry and quantitative methods. These contributions do not build the sustained chemical theory, synthesis and measurement at the centre of this degree. We therefore show Radboud’s curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a sufficiently close alternative.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary full-time Chemistry bachelor; 36 EC all-BC1 example
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 126 EC of required courses, 36 EC of conditioned scientific choice, a 12 EC individual research internship and 6 EC of free choice. The displayed choice is one permitted BC1 example, not a set of universally required courses; options may not run every year. Internship entry requires 120 EC including all first-year courses and prior proposal approval. First-year Academic Skills carries no extra credits; RADAr participation is required, but a passing score is not. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 39 EC. Course entry, attendance, overlap and approval rules apply.
